newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds static, spread to bund seen closing.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds static, spread to bund seen closing.

text.p: Danish bond prices showed little movement in early Thursday trade but dealers said that there was plenty of liquidity available and a rise was likely.

At 0745 GMT the benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 traded at 112.31, yielding 6.12 percent, from Tuesday's 112.35. The seven percent 2007, due to become the benchmark on September 1, was unchanged at 104.95, yielding 6.32 percent.

The 2006 bond's yield gap to the 10-year bund was static at 44 basis points but the 2007 gap to the bund shrank by one, to 64 basis points. The crown weakened marginally, to 3.8083 to the mark from 3.8081.
The dealer said that the past few days had seen a flattening of the yield curve toward the long end.
"We have seen the curve flatten between the two year and 10-year. The spread between the them has narrowed over the past few days to 216 bp from 220," he said.

He added that he expected the central bank to exploit the market liquidity and attempt to sell bonds. On Wednesday, he said, the bank sold 900 million crowns worth of two to 10-year paper. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
